newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria offers 12-mth floater T-bills, halts 9-mth.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria offers 12-mth floater T-bills, halts 9-mth.

text.p: Bulgaria's Finance Ministry will offer on Monday 20 billion levs of 12-month floating interest T-bills and will halt nine-month issues from next week, a central bank official said on Friday.

"Nine-month T-bills will not be offered any longer because it is more difficult for investors to accept this maturity," Nikolina Micheva, head of State Credits departments at the central bank told Reuters.
The par of the issue was raised from seven billion levs this week in line with Finance Ministry plans to issue longer maturities in the second half of 1997 to ease domestic debt payments.

Halting nine-month issues also reflected Finance Ministry's plans to place fewer issues with higher par values to enable more institutions qualify at the auctions and boost trade on the secondary market of treasury securities.
Interest on the issue is due at maturity. It equals the central bank main interest rate and is adjusted every time the rate is changed by the central bank.

The central bank advised banks earlier on Thursday it will cut its main rate from Monday to an effecive annual 16.30 percent calculated through the accumulation of monthly accruals from 42.24 percent now, dealers said.
